## Primary record

- DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-024-02574-2
- PMID: 39815104
- Article: *Resolving tissue complexity by multimodal spatial omics modeling with MISO*
- Official code: https://github.com/kpcoleman/miso
- Catalog entry: `MISO_2025`
- Local entry: `python/10_miso_manifest.py`

## What problem does it address?

MISO integrates and clusters multimodal spatial omics data, including transcriptomics with histology, chromatin/transcriptome measurements, spatial CITE-seq and spatial metabolomics examples.

## Minimal input contract

1. Two or more modalities with a shared spot/cell identifier.
2. Explicit coordinate convention and aligned image/feature extraction, when used.
3. A pinned Python 3.7 environment and Git-LFS weights, with preprocessing and modality QC recorded.

## Interpretation boundary

Integrated clusters are candidate spatial domains. They do not by themselves prove cell-cell signaling, causal tissue organization or a disease mechanism. Compare with modality-specific clustering and spatial neighborhood summaries.

## Reproduction status

The personal catalog currently creates a manifest and checks paths. It does not download Git-LFS weights or claim that the official MISO tutorial has been rerun.
